data.name: Luxor 2
data.detailed_description:
A muito esperada sequela do jogo casual #1 de 2005, LUXOR 2 muda a maneira de ver os puzzles de ação. LUXOR 2 leva-te numa bela viagem pelos 88 novos e magníficos níveis situados nas pirâmides do antigo Egipto. Usa o teu místico escaravelho para disparares e destruíres as esferas mágicas que se aproximam, e para te ajudar a destruí-las, Luxor 2 possui os "power-ups" mais explosivos de sempre.
  • 88 explosivos, desafiantes e magníficos níveis renderizados em 3D, levando os jogos casuais a outro nível
  • Quatro incríveis níveis de dificuldade, incluindo o nível profissional que desbloqueia o alucinante Desafio de Horus
  • Mais de 80 novas estatísticas e emblemas, com rondas bónus no fim de cada nível
  • Novo sistema de ranking para que os jogadores evoluam desde Farm Hand até Pharaoh
  • Três estimulantes modos de jogo, incluindo o novo modo de Sobrevivência e de Prática
  • 13 explosivos e únicos "power-ups", incluindo os novos Color Cloud, Net, Dagger e Lightning Storm, para ajudar na destruição das esferas inimigas que se aproximam
  • 13 intensas e compensadoras rondas bónus no final de cada nível do jogo

reviews.review:
'Luxor 2' is a classic Egyptian-themed casual action-puzzle game where players shoot colored spheres to create match-three chains and destroy advancing marble tracks before they reach the pyramids

This is my FAVORITE 'LUXOR' GAME ever! It's in fact my favorite marble-shooter game ever, yeah, I'm not a Team 'Zuma', I love 'Luxor' more, especially 'Luxor 2', but I still like 'Zuma', too, don't get the wrong idea. It's nostalgic, simple, and incredibly addictive. There's a great stage variety, and satisfying power-ups. 'Luxor 2' also introduced 3D levels (they're basically movies behind/under the marbles and PC, but still, for its time they were AAA level 3D designs), better physics, better controls, better maps, better story (the last "Set's Temple" map is a 'Papyrus' cartoon level evil Set; I love when media portrays Set really evil, not some strong guy), and MOST IMPORTANTLY, the thing that made 'Luxor 2' the pinnacle of the franchise, LIFETIME STATISTICS! The devs went all the way OCD-friendly mode and added statistics for literally anything: how many marbles you destroyed for each color, how many power-ups you took, how many wins/losses you got for each map, how many times you completed story mode for each difficulty, how many global points you earned, and etc., and etc. If I knew this day will come, I would've kept my save file from early 2000s.

One of my problems with this game is that the devs abandoned it and didn't renew the files for newer systems; since Flash was discontinued, so did these retro games that were based on Flash. Another one is that the devs abandoned this game, too: they didn't implement Steam Cloud feature for this game, so if you want to keep your stats forever, you'll need to move your save file between your PCs. Surprisingly, 'Rockstar' is also lazy when it comes to this, they also don't have Steam Cloud for any of their games (from the very first 'GTA' till 'GTA V'), which is weird, because 'GTA' games was always popular because of their extremely detailed statistics; it really would be cool to save those stats forever.

EDIT (26.10.2026): Although, I don't remember this being a case when I played it as a kid, but it seems the devs mixed up stats for marbles destroyed for orange and turquoise. Another reason I am adding this info because I don't forget it in the future, when I return to this game and look at my lifetime stats.
